findings.reason: the section should cite repair.py as the mechanism it extends, so the new durable write-back reads the id and the two action words from the existing owner rather than re-deriving them.
findings.text: §2 states code reviews "have a store but no answer field" and proposes adding that answer record, but names no owner for the finding identity and answer vocabulary it depends on: `reckon/crew/repair.py` already mints a stable per-finding id (`finding_id`, derived from file/line/text) and teaches the repair manifest to answer each finding as `acted <id>: <commit>` or `declined <id>: <reason>` (`compose_repair_brief`, repair.py:370-416)

findings.reason: naming repair.py (and plan_review.record_response) as the owner to extend turns §2 into a durable write-back of an existing vocabulary onto the ledger row, instead of a parallel answer store that can disagree with the one the repair is taught.
findings.text: the answer vocabulary (`ACTED_ACTION`/`DECLINED_ACTION`, taken from the shared `RESPONSE_ACTIONS`) and the finding-id scheme (repair.py:85) live in repair.py, and the plan-review store's `record_response` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:537`) is the sibling owner of the same `{action, reason, by, when}` response shape; if §2 defines its own "answer record" and its own parser for the manifest's `acted`/`declined` lines it forks that vocabulary, and a second spelling of "acted" drifts from the brief `compose_repair_brief` teaches the repair to emit

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the remaining work adds a write-back onto the existing review/ledger path; it introduces no new module and spreads no new interface over the machinery it extends.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the answer vocabulary and finding-identity scheme §2 needs are already owned by `reckon/crew/repair.py`; a second record that re-spells them forks the owner.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 proposes a new "answer record for code reviews" without citing `reckon/crew/repair.py`, which already mints the stable code-review finding id and defines the second-action answer vocabulary.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §2 reuses the existing stored-brief carrier (`a-worker-can-take-a-brief`) rather than wrapping it, and adds no forwarding rule it does not justify.
